hero.lead: A nation of 38.4 million between the Atlantic and the Atlas, trusted with a $4.5 billion IMF Flexible Credit Line and building one of Africa’s largest clean-energy systems.

capital.heading: Morocco borrows on the strength of its policies. Next, a safe toilet in every home.

record.text: IMF Flexible Credit Line: SDR 3.45 billion, precautionary, from 2 April 2025; access maintained at the review of 20 March 2026
Treasury debt, percent of GDP, end 2025: 1,145.0 billion dirhams, from 67.0% at end 2024
International bond in two euro tranches, priced 19 May 2026, with an order book of €5.2 billion
First Jobs and Green Growth Development Policy Loan, April 2026: over 330,000 job seekers reached by 2029
Ifahsa Pumped Hydropower Storage Project, July 2026: 300 MW that lets the grid take in at least 1 GW more solar and wind

register.name: International bond, two euro tranches
register.detail: Priced 19 May 2026 · €1.25 billion, 8 years, coupon 4.750% · €1 billion, 12 years, coupon 5.125% · Order book €5.2 billion
register.note: Yields 4.842% and 5.289%
register.text: The Moroccan Treasury raised €2.25 billion on the international market in two euro tranches, with an order book of €5.2 billion, more than twice the amount. Treasury borrowing funds the budget behind schools, clinics and water systems.
by: Ministry of Economy and Finance of Morocco

register.name: International bond, two euro tranches
register.detail: Issued 26 March 2025 · €900 million, 4 years, coupon 3.875% · €1.1 billion, 10 years, coupon 4.750% · Order book above €7 billion
register.note: Order book more than three times the issue
register.text: A two-tranche euro bond of the Moroccan Treasury, with an order book above €7 billion.
by: Ministry of Economy and Finance of Morocco

register.name: Ifahsa Pumped Hydropower Storage Project
register.detail: Approved 1 July 2026 · IBRD, Clean Technology Fund, Livable Planet Fund and ESMAP · Co-financed by the AfDB
register.note: 300 MW near Chefchaouen; about 820 direct jobs a year in construction
register.text: A 300-megawatt pumped storage plant, implemented by ONEE, that stores power so the grid can take in at least 1 gigawatt of additional solar and wind energy. Stored clean power keeps electricity steady for homes, clinics and water pumping.

register.name: Climate and Risk Finance Program
register.detail: Approved 12 June 2026 · Over five years
register.note: Up to $400 million private capital; $1 billion of pre-arranged disaster financing
register.text: Builds insurance and pre-arranged financing for disasters, extends cyber risk cover to at least 20 financial entities and draws up to $400 million of private capital into climate investment. Money in place before a disaster lets homes and services be rebuilt quickly.

register.name: Digital Transformation Acceleration Program
register.detail: Approved 12 June 2026 · Results by 2031
register.note: Close to $200 million private capital for start-ups and small firms
register.text: Supports digital public services and skills and, through government risk-sharing, draws close to $200 million of private capital into start-up finance and the digitisation of small firms. Digital services bring education, health and work within reach.

register.name: First Jobs and Green Growth Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Approved 10 April 2026 · First of a series of three
register.note: Over 330,000 job seekers reached by 2029
register.text: Backs reforms for private investment, clean energy, energy efficiency and exports, with targets that include more than 40,000 new childcare places and 1,200 direct jobs for women in childcare. Jobs are the livelihood standard.

register.name: Livable Planet Fund grant, Transforming Agri-food Systems Program
register.detail: Announced 18 December 2025 · Grant
register.note: About 1,200 farmers on 20,000 hectares
register.text: A grant that adds to the World Bank’s agri-food programme for climate-resilient farming. It reaches food and rural livelihoods.

register.name: Support to Strengthening of Social Safety Nets for Human Development
register.detail: Approved 19 June 2025
register.note: Direct Social Benefit programme: over 3.9 million households
register.text: Supports the Direct Social Benefit programme, which reached over 3.9 million households by March 2025. Cash support for families protects food, schooling and health.

register.name: Flexible Credit Line
register.detail: Approved 2 April 2025 · Two years · SDR 3.45 billion · Mid-term review completed 20 March 2026
register.note: Precautionary; current access maintained at the 2026 review
register.text: A precautionary IMF arrangement of SDR 3.45 billion, about $4.5 billion when approved, that Morocco can draw on if external shocks strike. It succeeded the arrangement of 2023.

register.name: Strengthening Human Capital for a Resilient Morocco, third operation
register.detail: Approved 19 March 2025 · Last in a series of three
register.note: Health, early childhood, older people and climate risk
register.text: Supports resilience to health risks, human capital in early childhood, lower poverty among older people and better management of climate risk. It reaches the health and livelihood standards.

register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: Approved September 2023 · Third and final review completed 17 March 2025 · SDR 937.5 million disbursed
register.note: 6 of 7 reform measures implemented
register.text: IMF financing for climate reforms. Morocco implemented six of the seven scheduled measures; the gradual introduction of a carbon tax was not implemented.

register.name: Transforming Agri-food Systems Program
register.detail: Approved 19 December 2024 · With a $5 million Livable Planet Fund grant
register.note: 1.36 million people, including almost 120,000 farmers
register.text: Builds the climate resilience of agriculture and the quality of food production, reaching farmers and more than one million consumers. It is the food standard.

register.name: Second Identity and Targeting for Social Protection Project
register.detail: Approved 4 December 2024
register.note: Population and social registries
register.text: Extends the National Population Registry, launches the National Register Agency and strengthens the Social Registry, so that vulnerable households, including in rural and remote areas, reach social programmes.

register.name: Municipal Solid Waste Management Support Program
register.detail: Approved 26 November 2024
register.note: Cities home to more than 60% of Moroccans
register.text: Upgrades controlled landfills, extends waste recovery and closes and rehabilitates abandoned uncontrolled landfills. Clean cities protect water and health.

register.name: State-owned enterprise reform and public sector performance (ENNAJAA)
register.detail: Approved 24 June 2024 · SOE reform $350 million · ENNAJAA additional financing $250 million
register.note: Governance of state-owned enterprises and public services
register.text: Supports the governance, restructuring and performance of state-owned enterprises, and a more digital, transparent public administration. The state companies run much of the water, power and transport behind the seven standards.

register.name: Economic Governance and Climate Resilience Programme, phase III (PGRCC III)
register.detail: Approved in Abidjan, reported 22 October 2026
register.note: State companies, partnerships, water and electricity governance
register.text: Supports the restructuring of the state-owned company portfolio, a modern framework for public-private partnerships and a better business climate, and modernises the governance of the water and electricity sectors for a low-carbon transition.

register.name: Airport Infrastructure Expansion and Modernization Programme (PEMIA)
register.detail: Signed 29 September 2026 · Loan to the National Airports Office (ONDA)
register.note: Marrakech, Agadir, Tangier and Fez airports
register.text: Expands and modernises four airports. Tourism and trade through these airports carry jobs across the regions they serve.

register.name: ONEE water production programme
register.detail: Announced 28 July 2026 · €120 million committed · €130 million uncommitted · €5 million grant · Guaranteed by Tamwilcom
register.note: The first EBRD loan in Morocco with a Tamwilcom guarantee
register.text: Finances ONEE’s nationwide programme to make water production more efficient and resilient: fewer losses, rehabilitated and expanded infrastructure and digital network management. In a nation below the water scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres a person, it is the water standard.

register.name: Fonds d’Équipement Communal, second loan
register.detail: Signed 22 July 2026 in Rabat
register.note: Rural roads, drinking water, urban renewal and schools
register.text: A loan to the public bank that finances local authorities, for rural access roads, drinking water networks, urban renewal and educational and socio-cultural facilities.

register.name: Rail Infrastructure Development Support Project (PADIF)
register.detail: Approved 8 July 2026 in Abidjan
register.note: Kenitra to Marrakech corridor
register.text: Extends the high-speed line and upgrades existing rail on the Kenitra to Marrakech corridor, with new rails, switches and project support.

register.name: Rail rehabilitation and motorway resilience
register.detail: Signed 30 June 2026 · ONCF €50 million and an EU grant of €15 million · ADM €300 million
register.note: Railways and motorways
register.text: Two EIB loans, to the national railway (ONCF) for rehabilitation and to the motorway company (ADM) for resilience. Reliable transport links citizens to jobs, schools and hospitals.

register.name: Cap Compétences 2030
register.detail: Announced 21 May 2026 · Results-based financing
register.note: Vocational training for young people and women
register.text: Finances a more relevant, varied and digital vocational training system linked to the job market. It reaches education and livelihood.

register.name: EIB financing signed in 2025
register.detail: Signed in 2025 · ONEE water €70 million · ONEE electricity €170 million · Post-earthquake reconstruction €500 million, second tranche of €1 billion
register.note: The largest EIB total for Morocco since 2012
register.text: Upgrades drinking water production and transmission, strengthens the power grid and rebuilds roads, schools and health facilities in the regions hit by the earthquake of 8 September 2023.

register.name: Conservation of Water Resources in the Saïss Plain (SAISS III)
register.detail: Signed 12 December 2025 in Rabat · Grants of €11.5 million
register.note: Over 20,000 hectares and 7,300 farms
register.text: Replaces overused groundwater with surface water from the M’Dez dam to protect the Saïss aquifer, with support for young people, women and small farmers. It is the final phase of the SAISS programme.

register.name: Partial credit guarantee for OCP Group
register.detail: Approved December 2025 · Non-sovereign guarantee of up to €450 million
register.note: Up to €530 million of long-term funding for green investment
register.text: Lets OCP raise long-term funding for its 2023 to 2030 Green Investment Programme: clean energy, water and energy efficiency, soil health and sustainable farming. The AfDB expects it to avoid more than 43 million tonnes of CO2 between 2026 and 2038.

register.name: Climate Operation, support to the Nationally Determined Contribution
register.detail: Approved 19 November 2025 · Sovereign · Co-finances a World Bank Program-for-Results
register.note: Weather radars, oases, date palms and argan
register.text: Finances weather radars and climate information, agricultural cooperatives in oasis areas, date palm processing, climate-resilient planting and the rehabilitation of traditional water systems.

register.name: Inclusive solidarity-based agriculture programme
register.detail: Announced 21 July 2025 · Loan
register.note: Women and young people in farming
register.text: Supports small farms facing climate change, food security, rural entrepreneurship and new farm infrastructure, in line with the National Solidarity Agriculture Program.

register.name: PGRCC II and PAFE-Emplois
register.detail: Announced 30 June 2025 · PGRCC II €181.8 million · PAFE-Emplois €119 million
register.note: Climate resilience and jobs through small enterprises
register.text: Two operations: economic and climate resilience with upgrades to the water and power sectors, and job creation through entrepreneurship and very small and medium-sized enterprises.

register.name: ONEE electricity, sustainability-linked loan
register.detail: Signed 20 June 2025 · The first sustainability-linked loan in the energy sector of the Middle East, North Africa and Africa
register.note: Targets: lower carbon intensity, more renewable power
register.text: Strengthens ONEE’s finances, with targets to cut the carbon intensity of electricity and raise the renewable share of output, towards the national goal of 52 per cent of installed capacity from renewables by 2030.

register.name: Green and resilient ports programme
register.detail: Authorised by the AFD Board 21 May 2026 · Concessional loan · EU grant €13.2 million · Blue Mediterranean Partnership grant €2 million
register.note: Rehabilitation and greening of ports, 13 named
register.text: A concessional loan to the National Ports Agency (ANP) to rehabilitate and green its ports. Fishing and trade ports carry coastal livelihoods.

register.name: KfW financing agreements
register.detail: Signed 16 December 2025 · Climate policies II €100 million · Social protection II €150 million · ONCF Casablanca-Settat rail €200 million
register.note: Climate, social protection and regional rail
register.text: Three agreements: climate adaptation and a low-carbon economy, the Direct Social Assistance programme and jobs for young people, and rail in the Casablanca-Settat region.

register.name: Agricultural Water Development in the Southeast Gharb Plain
register.detail: Signed 20 November 2025 · 2.2% a year · 30 years with 10 years of grace
register.note: Maximum JPY 64,577 million
register.text: A JICA loan for main canals, a pump station, a reservoir and equipment to irrigate the Sidi Kacem and Sidi Slimane provinces. Irrigation secures food and farm livelihoods.

register.name: New generation fishing port at Souiria K’dima
register.detail: Signed 6 February 2025 · Grant
register.note: JPY 2,003 million
register.text: A JICA grant for a new breakwater, seawall, landing wharf and fish handling area, and an ice-making machine. It supports the livelihoods of fishing families.

register.name: Development Policy Loan for Universal Health Coverage
register.detail: Signed 20 September 2024 · Co-financed with the World Bank ($500 million), the AfDB (€87 million) and AFD (€150 million)
register.note: Maximum JPY 27,760 million
register.text: A JICA policy loan towards universal health coverage, improving maternal and child health and nutrition services and financial protection in health. It is the health standard.

register.name: Pickalbatros hotels
register.detail: Announced 15 October 2026 · IFC $165 million · Attijariwafa bank $85 million
register.note: More than 1,350 direct jobs expected by 2032
register.text: Finances Pickalbatros’s Moroccan subsidiaries to buy three hotels in Casablanca and renovate properties, with about 6,200 indirect jobs also expected. Tourism jobs are livelihoods.

register.name: Tamwilcom, risk-sharing facility
register.detail: Announced 17 April 2026 · Unfunded risk-sharing facility · About $300 million
register.note: Covers SME guarantees already issued by Tamwilcom
register.text: IFC shares the risk on a portfolio of guarantees issued by Tamwilcom, the national credit guarantee institution, so that it can guarantee more loans, with women-owned businesses, farm enterprises and supply-chain firms as priorities.

register.name: Yakeey, Series A
register.detail: Announced 27 January 2026 · IFC equity in a $15 million round
register.note: IFC’s first venture investment in Moroccan real estate
register.text: IFC invested in Yakeey, a Casablanca platform that joins property search, valuation, brokerage and financing, with a network of more than 800 independent agents, nearly half of them women.

register.name: Saham Bank, unfunded risk participation
register.detail: Announced 3 November 2025 · Covers half of a $500 million-equivalent portfolio of corporate loans
register.note: Finance for Moroccan businesses
register.text: IFC takes on up to half of the credit risk on Saham Bank corporate loans, freeing the bank to lend more to businesses that create jobs.

register.name: Casablanca desalination plant
register.detail: Financing signed 8 May 2025 · 80% debt, 20% equity · Completion scheduled for 2028 · About €613 million
register.note: 300 million cubic metres a year for 7.5 million people
register.text: The Al Baidaa Desalination Company (ACCIONA 50%, Green of Africa 45%, AfriquiaGaz 5%) is building the plant, scheduled for completion in 2028, with debt from lenders including FIEM, COFIDES, Attijariwafa Bank, Banque Centrale Populaire and Bank of Africa. It will supply drinking water to 7.5 million people.

register.name: Kazyon, discount food retail
register.detail: Announced 11 March 2025 · Loan
register.note: More than 3,000 direct jobs expected
register.text: An IFC loan to expand Kazyon, a discount grocer with more than 150 stores in Morocco. Low-price food stores reach the food standard.

register.name: Al Amana Microfinance, Youth in Business
register.detail: Announced 24 January 2025 · Loan of up to €20 million
register.note: Small businesses led by people under 35
register.text: An EBRD loan for Al Amana to lend on to small businesses owned or led by young people, with a focus on the areas hit by the 2023 earthquake. It is the livelihood standard.

register.name: Tanger Med truck and passenger terminal
register.detail: Announced 4 November 2024 · IFC up to €197 million · Banks led by JP Morgan up to €203 million · MIGA guarantee up to 15 years
register.note: Truck capacity above 1 million units
register.text: Expands the truck and passenger terminal of the Tanger Med port complex, which handled 477,000 trucks in 2023. IFC called its loan the first sustainability-linked loan in Morocco.

register.name: Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, Rabat campus
register.detail: Announced 25 September 2024 · MIGA guarantee of €243.2 million (about $270 million) on loans to OCP Group
register.note: 5,684 students, including 721 PhD students
register.text: MIGA guarantees loans from Crédit Agricole CIB and Société Générale to OCP Group to expand the UM6P campus in Rabat with academic, sports and residential buildings and a 1,500-seat conference centre. It is the education standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 63 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Olive groves and green terraced fields in the foothills of the Atlas, Morocco

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Cedar forest in the Middle Atlas, Morocco

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Below the scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres: every drop must be stored, treated and reused.
items.alt: A reservoir behind a dam in the Atlas Mountains, Morocco

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: The Noor Ouarzazate concentrated solar power complex in the Moroccan desert

items.name: Kazyon
items.text: A discount grocer with more than 150 stores in Morocco, part of the largest discount retailer in the Arab world and Africa. IFC lent it US$30 million in March 2025, with more than 3,000 direct jobs expected.

items.name: Yakeey
items.text: A Casablanca platform that joins property search, valuation, brokerage and home financing, with more than 800 independent agents, nearly half of them women. IFC invested in its US$15 million Series A in January 2026.

items.name: ACWA Power
items.text: A power developer with seven projects in Morocco and 765 MW of installed capacity, representing nearly US$3.2 billion of investment. In August 2025 it signed 30-year contracts for Noor Midelt II and III, 800 MW of solar power with battery storage.

items.name: Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P)
items.text: A university with 5,684 students, including 721 doctoral students. A MIGA guarantee of €243.2 million in September 2024 backs the expansion of its Rabat campus.

items.name: Al Amana Microfinance
items.text: A microfinance institution with 2,400 employees and 647 branches, from the largest cities to the most isolated areas. The EBRD lent it up to €20 million in January 2025 for small businesses led by people under 35.

coverage.gap_text: Moroccans without a safely managed toilet at home: 92 in every hundred.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: Lenient measure: 6.5% are undernourished; food insecurity experience is not published

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: 97% cook with clean fuels and technology

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 40.2% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school; 2021

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above US$4.20 a day; 11.6% live below it, dated
